solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level fusion: synchronised NIR reflection and Raman spectra merged into one augmented matrix, as in the published feed-frame work. Both probes must sample the same powder spot, and data must be normalised to a common time step with block scaling so neither method dominates. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs or the extra instrument is dropped.

citations.quote: Data processing for pharmaceutical tasks relies on "low-level data fusion," where the synchronized NIR and Raman spectra are merged into a single augmented matrix.
the measurement data must be normalized to a common time step.

chemometrics_note: A PLS calibration or classification model per method is needed because NIR and Raman bands overlap in real blends; reference assay data from representative batches is the limiting resource, and validation on held-out batches is essential before any production claim.
realtime_tracking_note: The goal is time-resolved tracking of API concentration in the feed frame; acquisition rate and data synchronisation to a common time step should be fixed during the pilot so concentration changes are not blurred by averaging.
future_direction: If the pilot succeeds, a compact customized spectral fiber sensor or IoT-style sensor for the feed frame could be considered as a later step, as suggested in the AFS pathway material.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the required accuracy is modest and NIR reflection alone meets it on held-out batches, O1 suffices; if neither single method meets the target, the fused option O3 becomes the route.
proposal.next_step: Run the multi-method lab pilot on representative blend samples with independent reference assays, then a short feed-frame trial against customer-agreed go/no-go criteria.

brief_answer: Test NIR diffuse reflection first: it is the standard fiber-probe route for opaque powders and has published feed-frame precedent for blend potency. Compare it with a Raman fiber probe on the same blend; combine the two only if a single method misses your accuracy target. Open points: your API range and accuracy needs, excipient interferences, and the reference lab method for calibration.
